title: A bunker on the summit edge, above the clouds, Núi Bà Đen
description: A soldier in a bush hat sits on a sandbag-walled bunker with a pale covered roof at the edge of the summit, holding a red-and-white striped pole. A slope of crushed rock and red earth runs down to it, with cut stumps and a wire line at right, and beyond the position a sea of cloud lies below, the plain showing through at right. "The mountain is 2970 feet with the cloud general lower than the Mountain or right on us" — and when the cloud was on them, he says, they could see nothing.
researchNotes: Larry's comment of 2026-09-12 (giscus-vn-0036-c18416104.json). His 2,970 feet is recorded as given. The 1:50,000 sheet of the massif marks the summit spot height 986 (metres, about 3,235 feet; sources/map-l7014-6231-4-tay-ninh), and a 1969 release gives 3,200 feet (research/photos/nara-film-of-the-mountain.md); his figure is within a few hundred feet of both and is not corrected. The soldier on the bunker is not named, and what the striped pole was for is not on record.
